_comment_registration: Self-service sign-up is for retail customers only. New users get the customer role through defaultRole below. Business accounts are onboarded through services/identity, and staff accounts are created by an administrator. Users created in the admin console also receive default roles, so remove 'customer' from a staff account when creating it. Realm-import seed users are not given default roles. verifyEmail is off only because local dev has no SMTP server; turn it on wherever SMTP exists.
_comment_loginTheme: infra/keycloak/themes/damp is mounted at /opt/keycloak/themes/damp (docker-compose.yaml). It styles login, register, OTP, password reset and the error/info pages with the same tokens as frontend/shared/src/styles/theme.css.
_comment_roles: roles.realm is injected from shared/authz/generated/keycloak-roles.json by `make keycloak-realm` — see permissions.yaml, the single source for DAMP's RBAC model. Do not hand-edit a roles list here; it will be overwritten. roles.client is NOT overwritten: the client roles below are the service-to-service RBAC model (H2 core-ledger, H3 every other receiver), whose source of truth is this template and each service's route table (core-ledger/internal/api/auth.go, the Node ServiceAuthGuard's role decorators).

client._comment_h3_roles: H3: one bearer-only resource client per receiver service, holding the client roles that answer 'who is this caller' on that receiver. `<svc>.user-proxy` is granted to svc-bff alone — it is the ONLY role allowed to assert end-user identity headers. _comment_groups: Orgs live under /orgs/<slug> as Groups, created at runtime by services/identity when an organization is onboarded (POST to the Keycloak Admin API) — not seeded here. The parent group exists so every org has a consistent path prefix and so the org_id attribute mapper below has somewhere to read from. damp-demo-co is one seed example so 'company@damp.local' below has an org_id to log in with.

clients.name: DAMP Self-Service portal
clients.description: Public SPA client — matches frontend/public/runtime-config.js. PKCE pre-configured; directAccessGrantsEnabled stays on until authUtils.ts migrates off password grant (see docs/building-plan.md P1).
clients._comment_description: Kept under Keycloak's 255-char DESCRIPTION column limit (a dev-mode H2 schema constraint that bit the first, longer draft of this string) — see docs/building-plan.md's P1 note on migrating grant_type:'password' to auth-code+PKCE for the full rationale.

protocolMappers.name: aud-mapper-damp-portal
protocolMappers._comment: Mandatory — see docs/building-plan.md's P1 section. Without this, Keycloak issues aud: ["account"] for a public client and services/auth-proxy's JWT verification rejects every request. This is 'the single most likely day-one bug' per the plan.

protocolMappers.name: org-id-group-attribute
protocolMappers._comment: org_id is set on the user (copied from their org Group's org_id attribute by services/identity at membership time), not read live from group membership on every token issuance — a user can belong to exactly one primary org for token purposes.

clients.name: DAMP Ops Console
clients.description: Public SPA client for frontend/ops-console (admin, compliance, treasury, auditor). PKCE S256 only, no password grant. Its aud mapper adds damp-portal so auth-proxy's single audience check accepts its tokens.

protocolMappers.name: aud-mapper-damp-portal
protocolMappers._comment: auth-proxy verifies aud=damp-portal (OIDC_AUDIENCE). Both SPA clients put that audience in their tokens, so one gateway serves both apps. Each app still checks the user's roles itself before it renders anything.

protocolMappers.name: org-id-group-attribute
protocolMappers._comment: org_id is set on the user (copied from their org Group's org_id attribute by services/identity at membership time), not read live from group membership on every token issuance — a user can belong to exactly one primary org for token purposes.

_comment_clientScopeMappings: identity-service's service account HAS these realm-management roles via users[].clientRoles below, but fullScopeAllowed:false on the client means having a role isn't enough for it to appear in that client's own tokens — it also needs an explicit scope mapping granting it permission to include them. Without this, KeycloakAdminClient.getUser()/getUserGroups() 403 and JIT provisioning (services/identity/src/provisioning) can never complete a first login. The core-ledger block is the same rule for H2's service-to-service roles: each svc-* service account holds its role via users[].clientRoles, and this mapping is what lets the role appear in the token it mints (resource_access.core-ledger.roles).

clientScopeMappings._comment_h3_scope_mappings: The H3 receivers' scope mappings, same rule as core-ledger's: each svc-* service account holds its role via users[].clientRoles, and this mapping is what lets the role appear in the token it mints (resource_access.<receiver>.roles). The mappings live on the client that requests the token, naming roles of the resource client.

_comment_users: Six seed users, one per DAMP role, for local dev/demo login (matches the P1 DoD in docs/building-plan.md: 'log in as customer@damp.local' / 'compliance@damp.local'), plus one synthetic service-account user per service client granting it its roles — that's how a client's service account gets roles in a realm import, there's no serviceAccountRoles field on ClientRepresentation itself. Password is the dev-only literal below for every human seed user — never used outside a local --import-realm bootstrap.
